comment: gregsbrain publish no source. Read from the installed 2.6.5 build alongside the maker's own PDF, whose URL is in the module's entry in plugin.json rather than at the top of it. The manual is written for the hardware and carries a VCV Rack Addendum at the end, which is where the double-click assignment gesture, the missing MIDI mode, the greyed-out Calibration page, the dead display dimming and the scroll-wheel capture all come from. THE PITCH RANGE DISAGREES WITH THE MANUAL. XVoxBSP::VoltPerOctave clamps the jack voltage to -4 and 4 before PitchMode::GetPitch multiplies by 1200 cents, so the shift stops at four octaves; the manual says five. The manual also says that selecting the 0V to 5V VPO Range normals an unpatched VPO jack to 3V and moves the zero point there. Nothing in this build does that: SetVPOBias has an empty body, SetVPOPolarity only stores a value at XVoxBSP+0xc0, and VoltPerOctave never reads it. Microtonal quantization multiplies the same clamped voltage by 100 rather than 1200. A pitch has to move more than 15 cents before the module acts on it. The two audio inputs are read with getVoltageSum, so a polyphonic cable is mixed down to one signal; the first is normalled into the second. The outputs are mono and are soft-saturated or hard-clipped at 0.95 of full scale depending on the Clipping setting on the Audio Settings page, then multiplied by 5. The maker's own port names are the tooltips and are worth reading: they name the four gate and volt-per-octave jacks by the colour of their dress nuts, which is how the display identifies the voices. One disagreement inside the manual itself: its Audio Settings page says the A Gain slider controls the upper audio input, while the port the maker names Audio In A is the lower of the two jacks and the one the code normals into the other.
